## Runways and Terminals at Eugene Airport?

Eugene Airport, also known as Mahlon Sweet Field, is equipped with two asphalt runways:

 Runway 16R/34L: Measures 8,009 feet (2,441 meters) in length.
 Runway 16L/34R: Measures 6,000 feet (1,829 meters) in length.

These runways accommodate a variety of aircraft operations, supporting both commercial and general aviation activities at the airport.

### Main Terminal [...] Eugene Airport (IATA: EUG) also known as Mahlon Sweet Field serves around 1.2 million passengers within the United States. The airport has an area of 2,600 acres and owns two runways. The airport is the 5th largest airport in the Pacific Northwest.  
  
The five top airline carriers by passenger share in Eugene Airport from April 2018 to March 2019, were Horizon Air (26.7%), SkyWest Airlines (24.5%), United Airlines (19.1%), Compass Airlines (16.8%), and Allegiant Air (12.6%). [...] Airport terminal

## What facilities does Eugene Airport provide?

Eugene Airport provides facilities and services to offer comfort and ease to its travellers. In total, the airport has 2 gates as well as restaurants and cafes at the airport terminal.

### Facilities include:

 A selection of shopping and dining places are available from restaurants, cafes and luxury and designer shops.

In 2005, the crosswind runway was removed and replaced with Runway 16L/34R, 6,000 feet (1,800 m) long parallel to the primary runway 16R/34L.
 United Airlines resumed Boeing 737 flights to San Francisco in March 2008 but ended them the following August.
 Delta Connection operated by ExpressJet Airlines flew Embraer ERJ-145s nonstop to Los Angeles until September 1, 2008, when Delta ended its contract with ExpressJet on the Eugene-LAX route. [...] During World War II, the airfield was used by the United States Army Air Forces. The December 1951 C&GS diagram shows three runways forming an asterisk: the 026-deg runway was 5,229 feet (1,594 m) in length, the 111-deg was 5,205 ft (1,586 m), and the 158-deg was 3,999 ft (1,219 m).
